name: Colgate Palmolive (India) Ltd
title: Colgate Palmolive (India) Ltd - 500830 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue up 9% to Rs 1,583 crore with domestic growth 9.2%, but full-year sales flat at Rs 5,984 crore; no capacity or capex signal, and management guides to balanced volume-price growth with EBITDA not guided.

triggers.quote: We are not seeing any let up in promotional intensity. The market continues to be competitive.

guidance.value: Stays in the range (no numeric range given)

summary.headline: Colgate India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 1,583 crore, with domestic growth at 9.2% and gross margin at 69.6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were Rs 1,583 crore, up 9% YoY, with domestic growth of 9.2% and growth broad-based across Core, Premium, toothpaste, toothbrush and personal care. Full-year FY26 sales were flat at Rs 5,984 crore, and full-year EBITDA margin was 31.2% including an 80 bps GST input-credit (IDS) impact. Q4 NPAT was Rs 353 crore, and excluding one-offs (restructuring, GST, prior-period tax refunds, labour code) management said profit grew about 9%. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 48 per share and said it is still paying out virtually 100% of NPAT.

financial_highlights.change: excluding one-offs, management says profit grew about 9%
absolute spend up 10%; FY26 13.7% of sales
stated as improved on prior years despite GST-blocked capital

segments.name: Toothpaste (Core: Colgate Strong Teeth, Max Fresh)
segments.commentary: Max Fresh is described as the fastest-growing franchise in the portfolio, with a blue variant in testing and new Sensorials variants (berry added). Management said consideration for all sub-brands is flat or rising versus original levels.

segments.name: Premium (Colgate Total, Visible White, PerioGard)
segments.commentary: Premium mix is up 35% over the past two years per management. Visible White Purple was launched 18 months ago and is described as the most successful launch in Colgate's history; PerioGard franchise is said to be doubling YoY. Management did not disclose the premium share of sales; e-commerce is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Toothbrush
segments.commentary: Management says Colgate is 1.7x its nearest competitor in the entry tier. New launches include a Rs 10 brush with 16g to 20g of toothpaste offered in the pack and a PerioGuard brush.

segments.name: Personal care (Palmolive)
segments.commentary: Palmolive focus is hand wash and body wash. Management said foaming hand wash is the leader in the category and growing at double digits in key channels; body wash is a partnership-led watch item.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin is expected to stay in the range seen in recent quarters over the next two quarters despite commodity and currency headwinds, offset by the Funding the Growth programme.
EBITDA is not guided to a specific level or expansion; it will be calibrated to advertising investment, with top-line growth and absolute profit as the stated priorities.
A price increase to offset the post-West Asia inflation is expected to be taken within a few weeks; category price increases are expected to be in the low single digits.
Management targets balanced volume and price-led growth but gave no numerical growth target.
Management is pursuing GST input-credit mitigation through supplier duty representations, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and transporter rate changes.
Brand investment is expected to rise further from the Q4 level of 12.6% of sales; FY26 was 13.7%.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Direct outlets reach is 1.7 lakh; 2 lakh stores were added to reach in 2025.
Plant sustainability: recyclable tubes now fully adopted, renewable energy share moved from 40% to 60%, plastic neutrality at 101%, recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging at 95%.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was balanced between price and volume, and management said Q4 volume was flat.
Post-GST price cuts have been lapped after the Q1 calendar 2026 anniversary, so the price increase is now needed for input-cost inflation.
Rural demand is recovering and is beginning to converge with urban growth, though rural is growing more slowly than in 2025.
Promotional intensity has not eased; management is using AI tools to cull promotions and redeploying the spend.
Premium portfolio is growing faster than the core; management cited the 130-140 index to the core as the premium threshold.
Quick commerce share is ahead of total e-commerce, which is ahead of the offline business.

qa_highlights.question: How has the QR-linked dentist recommendation programme helped premiumisation, and how is B2B sales to dentists growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4.5 million people were scanned, with around 20% of scans going to a dentist; the programme is being repeated and expanded to a virtual format via QR codes on 500 packs. B2B sales to the profession grew at about a 50-60% two-year CAGR, with a field force of about 150 people.

qa_highlights.question: Competitors have launched similar products (for example Purple); is the market expanding and what is the D2C threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Purple is accelerating and it aims to hold the largest share of the whitening segment. Most D2C brands are still small, and Colgate's quick-commerce share is ahead of its e-commerce share, so there is no loss of share.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing growth in Q4 from the price increase, and will the West Asia-linked inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 growth was about half price and half volume, with the post-GST price cuts now lapped. A price increase for inflation is expected within a few weeks; gross margin should stay in range but EBITDA will depend on advertising.

qa_highlights.question: How should volume growth be viewed going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is balanced volume and price growth, not reliance on price as in the past, and not relying too heavily on volume.

qa_highlights.question: How is premium defined and what share of sales does it represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium is defined as products at a 130-140 price index to the core range and outside Active Salt, Max Fresh and Cibac. Premium's contribution has risen 35% in two years; management declined to disclose the premium share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 EBITDA margin at a sustainable level, and is there room to expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin will keep improving through the Funding the Growth programme. It gave no EBITDA margin target, saying advertising spend is the key variable and top-line and absolute profit growth are the priorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the GST inverted duty structure and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 80 bps (full year) and 160 bps (Q4) IDS impact stays in the baseline. Mitigation includes lower GST on transport services, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and supplier representations for lower input GST.

qa_highlights.question: Did higher-grammage packs drive Q4 growth, and what is the top-line growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grammage increases of about 11% on a few packs were a pass-through of the GST cut, but were not the main driver of growth. 30-40% of SKUs are already higher-grammage. No numeric growth target was given; management stated top-line growth is a priority.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and currency costs, and the GST inverted duty structure (IDS) impact of 80 bps for FY26 and 160 bps in Q4.
Rising advertising intensity (Q4 12.6% of sales, FY26 13.7%) may keep EBITDA margins under pressure.
Competitive intensity in premium whitening, with copycat launches and D2C brands in toothpaste; promotional intensity has not eased.
Timing and size of the price increase for input-cost inflation; whether volume growth can be sustained alongside price.
Whether the rural demand recovery continues and whether the Q4 acceleration in growth holds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the brand, premium portfolio and cash generation, but cautious on FY27 margins, with no EBITDA guidance. Management was evasive on the premium share of sales and on the timing and size of pricing.

So, we obviously are looking to grow this company fast. Top-line growth remains a huge priority

growth.why: No numerical growth target was given; management targets balanced volume and price-led growth, with a low-single-digit category price increase coming within weeks, and no capacity or capex was disclosed, so the backing is vague.
